scope: Read-only current source audit; does not by itself identify the cause of the recorded run

cancel_chain.condition: Emergency state first escape tick calls callEmergencyStop, which publishes ACTION_ABORT and clears have_published_trajectory

Active goal and received action2/5 clears native, arm pieces, progress, pending; retains active goal. active and no path returns None before navigation kernel.plan; cancelled state is sticky until accepted new reference/finish/goal event.

cancelled is not in allowed reference_wait_hold reasons; None result leads reject, publishes zero base twist and no new arm target. It is classified reference transition, so this cancellation does not recursively publish another tracking fault.
Resumption requires a new non-stale valid native polynomial plus matching fresh progress/quiet interval; no reference-free navigation fallback exists.

possible_abort_sources_current_code.condition: new tracking fault -> zero safety owner + EMERGENCY_STOP
raw/live dynamic collision within dynamic_emergency_distance -> transient recovery -> EMERGENCY_STOP
actual hard collision, or failed static close collision repair -> EMERGENCY_STOP

refresh_chain.condition: intervention if nominal invalid or nominal external gap<0.12m; not necessarily dynamic obstacle. If all sampled candidates invalid, result None and no event.

Only after publishing arm and base topics; execute, active valid goal, not startup/wait_hold/terminal; true intervention needed. Delivery here is ROS publish after validations, not independent actuator execution acknowledgement.
Same goal and continuing interventions repeats same episode id. 4 delivered nominal cycles end episode. Failed cycles are not clearance. Next episode gets first checked_at timestamp.

Only unfinished EXEC_TRAJ with usable published reference and no recovery/fault/zero limit/unmetESDF/freshness guard; one attempt per episode even if failure; failed optional refresh restores old trajectory metadata rather than auto aborting it.
Goal/reference IDs must match; event age<=0.25s; odom/joint<=0.15s; map/required dynamic<=0.35s; episode not consumed.

interpretation: The early refresh path can be unavailable before a first intervention delivery, after cancellation, during delivery rejection, or while the slow layer owns a zero-speed recovery. In these cases existing slow recovery handles replanning; fast reference-free avoidance is not implemented.
An optional refresh itself does not mandate stopping. Slow safety independently evaluates its reference and can stop/cancel before or despite fast-layer intervention.
A zero safety limit zeros both base v/w at whole_body_mppi.py:755-762; with valid reference arm commands remain eligible, but cancellation additionally prevents new kernel planning.

Parent reported 744 cancelled statuses and 152 refresh messages in 4 episodes. These are not independently re-counted here. Cancelled status count does not count abort events, and refresh message/episode counts do not establish accepted/successful replans.
required_timeline_to_attribute: First ACTION_ABORT source and preceding planner log owner (TRACKING/SAFETY/PERCEPTION/ACTUAL_STATE).
Last successful fast command/intervention, first rejection, safety limit zero, and episode publish times versus abort.
FSM MPPIRefresh acceptance/success logs versus request identities; map/feedback ages if valid episodes were not consumed.
